newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World slumps on results report.
newsitem.headline: New World slumps on results report.

text.p: New World Development Ltd trended weaker on Friday following the release of its results for 1995/96 on Thursday which were slightly less than market expectations, brokers said.
New World Development lost HK$0.70, or 1.8 percent, to trade at HK$46.10 in Friday afternoon trading.

The company reported net profit of HK$4.16 billion for the year ended June 30, 1996, a 21.89 percent rise over the previous year. The latest Estimate Directory shows the consensus forecast had been at HK$4.28 billion.
Gilbert Chu, head of research at Crosby Securities, said New World's results were slightly disappointing but not significantly different from what he had forecast.
"New World has been running ahead but there are other reasons. I think the share has outperformed the market and it is bound to see some correction. I would not say it is unusual," he said.
Property analyst Manfred Ho at CEF GC Brokerage said New World was fully valued at this level.
"We estimate a net asset value of HK$46.00 for New World and, at yesterday's closing price, it is trading at a slight premium to that NAV," Ho said.
"Based on our estimates the share is also trading on a prospective price earnings ratio of 17 times 1997 earnings," he added.

Property analysts said that an increase in the plot ratio of buildings in Tsim Sha Tsui and other areas in Hong Kong's Kowloon district will benefit property companies, but added it was still too early to discount those gains.
